sections.title: From camera feed to validated production model

steps.title: Visual task definition and feasibility
steps.description: We define exactly what must be detected or measured, the acceptable error rates, latency and hardware constraints, and review sample imagery to confirm feasibility.

steps.title: Data collection and labeling
steps.description: We capture or curate imagery that reflects real operating conditions, label it with documented guidelines and hold out a representative test set.

steps.title: Model training and validation
steps.description: We train and compare architectures, then validate precision, recall and latency on the held-out set — including edge cases and failure analysis.

steps.title: Deployment, integration and monitoring
steps.description: Optimized inference on cloud or edge, integration with MES, ERP, PACS or your application, plus drift monitoring and an active-learning loop for retraining.

items.question: How much does computer vision development cost?
items.answer: Simple object detection starts at $40,000–$60,000. Manufacturing quality inspection typically runs $60,000–$130,000, and medical imaging AI $90,000–$200,000+. The training data situation is the biggest variable.

items.question: How many images do we need?
items.answer: A single-class detector in a controlled environment can often be trained on 2,000–5,000 labeled images. Multi-class detection in variable conditions usually needs 5,000–15,000. Rare defects can be supplemented with synthetic data and active learning.

items.question: Can the model run on edge devices?
items.answer: Yes. We optimize models with quantization and runtimes such as TensorRT and ONNX Runtime to run on NVIDIA Jetson, industrial PCs and smart cameras when latency, connectivity or privacy require on-device inference.

items.question: What accuracy can we expect?
items.answer: It depends on task difficulty and data quality. Well-defined detection tasks in controlled environments commonly reach 90–96% accuracy; high-precision inspection can exceed 99% precision with appropriate imaging. We agree on target metrics before build and report them on a held-out test set.

items.question: Do you use existing models or train from scratch?
items.answer: Usually we fine-tune proven pretrained architectures on your data, which reduces data requirements and cost. For document and open-ended visual questions we may use vision-language models instead of training a dedicated detector.

items.question: Who owns the trained model?
items.answer: You do — model weights, training code, labeled datasets and deployment configuration are transferred at completion.
